requirements.subject: ent:while-statement
requirements.canonical: A while statement IS a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.
requirements.original: A while statement defines a loop that is executed as long as the loop condition holds.

requirements.subject: ent:while-statement
requirements.canonical: The while statement has the syntax `while` "(" [(VarInstance | Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock.
requirements.original: while "(" [(VarInstance|Assignment) ";"] BooleanExpression ")" StatementBlock

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a while statement MAY be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment).
requirements.original: The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

requirements.subject: ent:init-statement
requirements.canonical: The init statement of a while statement IS executed before the loop condition is evaluated.
requirements.original: The loop condition may be preceded by an init statement (variable declaration or assignment), which executes before the expression is evaluated.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether the init statement executes once before the first evaluation or before every evaluation of the loop condition; chosen reading: once.
readings: The init statement of a while statement IS executed once, before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
The init statement of a while statement IS executed before each evaluation of the loop condition.

requirements.subject: ent:variable
requirements.canonical: The scope of a variable declared within the init statement of a while statement SHALL be limited to the while statement.
requirements.original: The scope of variables declared within an init statement shall be limited to the while statement.

requirements.subject: ent:loop-condition
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a while statement SHALL be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.
requirements.original: The loop condition shall be checked at the beginning of each new loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:while-statement
requirements.condition: the loop condition does not hold
requirements.canonical: If the loop condition of a while statement does not hold, the loop SHALL be exited and execution SHALL continue with the statement immediately following the while loop.
requirements.original: If the loop condition does not hold, then the loop is exited and execution shall continue with the statement, which immediately follows the while loop.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the while loop IS terminated.
requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: A do-while statement IS a loop that is executed until the loop condition does not hold.
requirements.original: A do-while statement defines a loop that is executed up until the loop condition does not hold.

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: The do-while statement has the syntax `do` StatementBlock `while` "(" BooleanExpression ")".
requirements.original: do StatementBlock while "(" BooleanExpression ")"

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: A do-while loop IS identical to a while loop except for the point at which the loop condition is checked.
requirements.original: The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:loop-condition
requirements.canonical: The loop condition of a do-while statement SHALL be checked at the end of each loop iteration.
requirements.original: The do-while loop is identical to a while loop with the exception that the loop condition shall be checked at the end of each loop iteration.

requirements.subject: ent:do-while-statement
requirements.canonical: The statement block of a do-while loop IS executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.
requirements.original: This means when using a do-while loop the behaviour is executed at least once before the loop condition is evaluated for the first time.

requirements.subject: ent:break-statement
requirements.condition: the break statement is not within an enclosed loop, alt, altstep or interleave
requirements.canonical: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt statement, altstep or interleave statement, the do-while loop IS terminated.
requirements.original: If a break statement is executed that is not within the body of an enclosed loop, alt, alststep or interleave, then the loop is terminated, too.

ambiguity.issue: The text uses the misspelling 'alststep' instead of 'altstep'.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.original: The label statement allows the specification of labels in test cases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: The label statement has the syntax `label` LabelIdentifier.
requirements.original: label LabelIdentifier

requirements.subject: ent:label
requirements.canonical: A label marks a statement.
requirements.original: A label marks a statement.

requirements.subject: ent:label
requirements.canonical: A label IS used by the goto statement to transfer control to the labelled statement.
requirements.original: The label is used by the goto statement (see clause 19.8) to transfer control to a labelled statement.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be used like any other TTCN-3 behavioural program statement according to the syntax rules of annex A.
requirements.original: a) A label statement can be used freely like other TTCN-3 behavioural program statements according to the syntax rules defined in annex A.

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement MAY be placed before or after a TTCN-3 statement.
requirements.original: It can be used before or after a TTCN-3 statement

requirements.subject: ent:label-statement
requirements.canonical: A label statement SHALL NOT be the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.
requirements.original: but not as the first statement of an alternative or top alternative in an alt statement, interleave statement or altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:label
requirements.canonical: A label defined by a label statement SHALL be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.
requirements.original: b) Labels used following the label keyword shall be unique among all labels defined in the same test case, function or altstep.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement performs a jump to a label.
requirements.original: A goto statement performs a jump to a label.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: The goto statement has the syntax `goto` LabelIdentifier.
requirements.original: goto LabelIdentifier

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.
requirements.original: The goto statement can be used in functions, test cases and altsteps to transfer control to a labelled statement.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump forwards and backwards within a sequence of statements.
requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump out of a single compound statement.
requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement MAY jump over several levels out of nested compound statements.
requirements.original: The goto statement provides the possibility to jump freely, i.e. forwards and backwards, within a sequence of statements, to jump out of a single compound statement (e.g. a while loop) and to jump over several levels out of nested compound statements (e.g. nested alternatives).

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump out of a function, test case or altstep.
requirements.original: a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into a function, test case or altstep.
requirements.original: a) It is not allowed to jump out of or into functions, test cases and altsteps.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (alt statement, while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop or interleave statement).
requirements.original: b) It is not allowed to jump into a sequence of statements defined in a compound statement (i.e. alt statement, while loop, for loop, if-else statement, do-while loop and the interleave statement).

ambiguity.issue: The list introduced by 'i.e.' omits select case and select union statements and plain statement blocks; chosen reading: the list is exhaustive.
readings: A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into the statements of an alt, while, for, if-else, do-while or interleave statement only.
A goto statement SHALL NOT jump into any compound statement, including select case and select union statements.

requirements.subject: ent:goto-statement
requirements.canonical: A goto statement SHALL NOT be used within an interleave statement.
requirements.original: c) It is not allowed to use the goto statement within an interleave statement.
